contrary_evidence: Visible Hormuz commodity-vessel traffic remains severely below recent averages despite partial Saudi export-logistics relief.
Refined-product markets, especially diesel, remain tight, so lower crude prices do not imply equivalent relief in transport or industrial fuel costs.
Public bank forecasts differ on the timing of the next Fed hike; the institutional consensus is therefore classified as Unclear rather than Broadening.
limitations: Kpler/Reuters Hormuz observations are preliminary snapshots whose cutoffs and/or classification states are not sufficiently comparable for a precise day-over-day throughput series, and AIS-dark traffic can be omitted.
Several intraday market prices are time-sensitive observations rather than official closes.
The energy-relief mechanism depends partly on expected restoration of Saudi pipeline capacity and therefore remains less certain than the observed monetary-policy change.
notes: Revision 1 resolves the prior QA blockers without changing the controlled program architecture. The prior rejection remains historical. Approval is valid only for the exact pending and source blob SHAs recorded here.

qa_fixes_applied: Downgraded institutional consensus state from Broadening to Unclear because only Goldman Sachs had a sufficiently attributable dated house-view change; Fed projections and market pricing are no longer counted as institutional research signals.

Reconciled Reuters/Kpler Hormuz observations: September 16 contemporaneous snapshot reported four Tuesday commodity-vessel transits versus a 10-day average of 18, while the September 17 0445 GMT snapshot reported three Wednesday transits versus a 10-day average near 17 and retrospectively cited 12 for Tuesday. The report now treats these as preliminary cutoff/classification-sensitive snapshots rather than a continuous day-over-day series.

Recalculated energy-relief confidence, scenarios and conclusions so they rely on Saudi alternative export loadings, expected East-West pipeline restoration and observed crude-price easing, while treating Hormuz evidence only as confirmation of severely depressed visible traffic.
